title: The Changing Landscape of Accrual Accounting

scopes.description: The complete author-documented workflow for reproducing the supplemental analyses in the Internet Appendix. Only the appendix PDF is supplied, so no executable entry point or complete dependency closure can be established.

requirements.description: Inputs sufficient to reproduce the appendix empirical analyses and their reported sample construction are required. The appendix describes annual firm-level analyses and reports sample periods and selected counts, but the package supplies no data or input specification; the compatible data product, identifiers, complete fields/history, transformations, and acquisition route remain undetermined. Model and formula references in this appendix do not by themselves establish separate mandatory raw-source dependencies.

issues.description: The assessed package contains only a supplemental-results appendix and no README/data description, executable author code, entry points, or workflow instructions. The full dependency closure and software requirements therefore cannot be determined.

evidence.description: The supplied document identifies itself as supplemental analysis to the main results and lists appendix sections.
evidence.quote: This appendix provides supplemental analyses to the main results presented in “The changing landscape of accrual accounting”. Content of the Internet Appendix: A1. Additional sample composition analysis

evidence.description: The appendix contents name two figures and two robustness tables as supplemental outputs.
evidence.quote: Figure IA1: A relatively constant sample: The levels model based on Dechow (1994)

evidence.description: The appendix reports annual Dechow-model subsample counts and sample years, confirming that these supplemental results depend on empirical observations.
evidence.quote: There are on average 1,018 and 558 observations per year from 1964 to 2014 when we require at least 30 and 40 years’ data for a firm to be included in these two subsamples, respectively, compared to 4,258 observations without such a requirement.

evidence.description: Table IA1 documents sample construction inputs and period for its regression analysis.
evidence.quote: The sample includes 159,932 firm-year observations with non-missing TACCi,t, CFOi,t-1 , CFOi,t and CFOi,t+1 from 1964 to 2013.

evidence.description: The frozen static audit inventory contains only the appendix PDF, with no entry points or dependency edges and coverage marked no_supported_code.

actions.description: Request the complete author replication workflow and a compatible input route for the appendix analyses.
steps: Request the complete author-provided replication package, or an approved replacement workflow, including entry points, supporting programs, software/version requirements, execution order, and a mapping from each listed appendix figure/table to the scripts that produce it.

Request the author-prepared analysis inputs or a verified acquisition route, with product/file format, identifiers, required columns, covered years, sample definitions, transformations, and any access conditions. Do not treat the cited model/formula names alone as proof of separate raw-source inputs.
After receiving the materials, trace the actual producer-consumer order and update the dependency closure and compatible input routes from that evidence.
validation: Confirm that every supplied appendix figure and table is mapped to an author entry point and that every required intermediate has a documented producer.
Confirm the supplied input route supports the documented variables, identifiers, sample construction, and reported periods before classifying it as compatible.
Only after a separate authorized execution, compare reproduced sample totals and appendix outputs with the author-reported periods and counts.

review_notes: This is an appendix-only release with no supplied author workflow. The cited model and formula names are context for clarifying the missing workflow; they do not automatically create distinct live raw-data requirements.
No analysis_only scope is supported because neither author code nor an author-prepared analysis-input route is supplied.
